newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Futures selling, end of account blues cap Bel-20.
newsitem.headline: Futures selling, end of account blues cap Bel-20.

text.p: Heavy hedge fund selling in the futures market and the imminent end of the account capped the early surge on the Brussels bourse on Tuesday despite the steep overnight rally in New York, traders said.

The Bel-20 blue chip share index was 6.63 points or 0.29 percent higher at 2,261.50 at 0900 GMT after opening at a new record high of 2,271.54 following the 143-point climb in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
"The Bel-20 stocks are blocked by the big futures order, so the market will stay at these levels until the account ends on Wednesday," one trader said.
The Brussels stock market is closed on Thursday for the Ascension Day holiday, but will be open on Friday.
Traders said that despite the fact that many stocks go ex-dividend on Friday the underlying mood of the market would be strong enough to push the index to new pinnacles.
"The market will move up from Friday," one trader said.

On Tuesday the main gainers were non-index stocks, particularly fast food chain Quick which rose 2.8 percent to 1,850 francs as one broker upgraded the share to hold from sell, prompting investors to focus on what has been a lagging share.
Electronics firm Barco also performed well despite being in the index, rising 0.8 percent to 6,200 francs after climbing at one stage to 6,270 francs.
"It would be even higher today if it were not in the index," one trader said.
Busiest share by value was steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, up 0.5 percent to 21,025 francs.
